stemBlocks.value: Rewrite 3x² + 18x + 20 in completed-square form, then determine the minimum value of the expression and the value of x at which the minimum occurs.
Think first: Once the expression is a(x + h)² + k, both answers are visible without any further calculation.

contentBlocks.value: half of 6 is 3, and 3² = 9, so x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the 3 through and combine constants.
Set the square to zero to locate the minimum.

strategyBlocks.value: Factor 3 from the x-terms, complete the square, then read the minimum as the constant k and its position from the bracket.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: 3x² + 18x + 20 = 3(x + 3)² − 7; the minimum value is −7 and it occurs at x = −3.

whyThisWorks.value: The term 3(x + 3)² is non-negative for every x, so the expression can never fall below −7. It reaches −7 exactly once, at the x that makes the bracket vanish. Multiplying by 3 stretches the parabola vertically but does not move its lowest point sideways, so the position of the minimum comes only from the bracket.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the minimum as −7 but the position as x = 3 instead of x = −3.
